Spine: as_is_workflow_v3; data: edges.json v0.5, timing.json v0.2
model, writes one sentence per edge
Stop nodes return control to the person with a question,
never with an answer the tool made up.
7 decisions, each a variable with options.
Editing means choosing another option; the
two scenarios differ only in what is active.
edge = {from, to, direction, lag, camp, claim_type, evidence, geography, source, fork}
7 mechanism · 4 theory · 19 observation · 4 forks kept unresolved
City requires a plan, records no return
fee to reserve to room: lag unknown
Three honest stops. The tool refuses
to draw a domino nobody has measured.
effect lands at t + lag, persists
Direction and lag only, no magnitudes.
in the script picks a winner.

Two runs, one edited option between them.
More than two is allowed; two is what the
tool the person operates: years on x, outcomes on y

every sourced effect on tenants is harm
the benefit arrives after the policy ends
Evaluation cases, checkable without the model
expected: e01, e29 (negative lag), e07 chain into health
expected: e27, e28, fork f4 drawn twice
expected: stop at check 1, ask for source
report: how much the sentences vary
real building file: fills the ? weeks on the as-is axis
tests the rerun loop on an option they actually chose
tests whether the forks read as fair to the party with no document
Every actor in the process produces a document: the owner an application, Council a permit, the architect drawings, the funder an agreement, the City a survey.
The tenant produces none and receives none. In six of seven permit files the tenants were gone before the application was filed.
The tool is the first point in the sequence where the tenant's timeline is drawn.
Delegated to the tool: loading, traversal, time placement, citation checking, rendering, pattern flags.
Kept with a person: which option, which horizon, which camps to show, whether to edit, what a flagged barrier means.
Never delegated: adding an edge, setting a lag, choosing a source. Those happen in edges.json, by hand, with the paper open.
Evidence is thin where the debate is loudest: three weak observation edges, all from one thesis. Two of four strong edges are from US cities.
No magnitudes anywhere; the tool shows direction and timing only. Four as-is durations are still unknown and wait on an operator's file.
The 200 sf rule is a live designation threshold, not a design standard; its effect on tenants has no source and the tool stops there.
